name: Dot population count
looks: A big number counts up while a population of small dots under it stands for the total, one dot per unit. A subset highlights in the accent colour to call out a slice, then the dots relax apart or gather into a ring whose arc-length per colour shows a breakdown, with small labels naming the outliers at the edges.
build: One dot per unit (or sampled with a label above a few hundred); grid positions with ±1-2px jitter so it never reads as a raster. Scatter state tweens each dot to `r = R*sqrt(random())`, `theta = random()*2PI` inside a soft circle. Ring state buckets dots by category along an arc proportional to its share. The count-up ties to the same clock as the dots.
sound: A soft granular patter while the dots settle, a tick on the count-up digits, a louder tick when the accent subset highlights.
prompt: Show a total as a population of small dots, one per unit, with the number counting up above it. Let a subset highlight in the accent colour to call out a slice of the total, then let the dots relax apart or regroup into a ring whose arcs show a breakdown by category, with a small label for whatever the main cluster doesn't cover.
